title: Special-point incidence on nodal components under closed-field extension
statement: Let $k\subseteq L$ be algebraically closed fields [def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-pc-field-extension]. Let $C$ be a finite type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], empty or pure of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension], such that every nonsmooth point [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] has completed local ring $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $i:F\hookrightarrow C$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and image in the smooth locus. Let $Z=\operatorname{Sing}(C/k)$ be the first-Fitting singular subscheme [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. Then $F$ and $Z$ are finite disjoint unions of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, their scalar extensions replace each copy by exactly one $\operatorname{Spec}L$, and $Z_L$ has support equal to the nonsmooth locus of $C_L=C\times_kL$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For any reduced irreducible component $R\hookrightarrow C$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] whose scalar extension is a reduced component of $C_L$, each point of $F\cup |Z|$ lies on $R$ if and only if its unique scalar-extended point lies on $R_L$. Consequently $|R\cap(F\cup |Z|)|=|R_L\cap(F_L\cup |Z_L|)|$. These are numbers of distinct points on the component itself; a self-node counts once, not twice as its two branches. No properness or separatedness is required; the marking and singular set can be empty.

source.place: Tag 0C59 (lemma-nodal-family), first-Fitting singular subscheme; morphisms.tex Tag 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field); returned Step 11, rational-point incidence under scalar extension.

proof.text: If $C$ is empty, its closed subschemes $F$ and $Z$ are empty, as are their base changes, and there is no component $R$; all assertions follow. Suppose henceforth that $C$ is pure of dimension $1$. Write $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. By [lem-pc-flat-field], $f$ is flat. The field $k$ is Noetherian since its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$, so [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes the finite-type $f$ locally finitely presented. Apply [lem-trf-chosen-nodal-fibres-universal] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and with $k$ itself as the chosen algebraic closure of its residue field. Its hypotheses are exactly the dimension and completed-local-ring assumptions on $C$. It gives pure dimension one and nodality for every nonempty geometric fibre of $f$, including extensions by algebraically closed fields.

source.place: Tag 0C56 (lemma-node-field-extension), as assembled in lem-trf-chosen-nodal-fibres-universal; flatness over a field and local finite presentation over a Noetherian field

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular] to $f$, whose flatness, local finite presentation and geometric-fibre assumptions were established in step 1. It states that $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is unramified and $|Z|$ is the complement of the smooth locus of $C/k$. Apply its arbitrary-base-change clause to $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: the first-Fitting singular subscheme of $C_L/L$ is canonically $Z\times_k L$, and its support is exactly the nonsmooth locus of $C_L/L$. Thus the symbol $Z_L$ denotes this actual scalar extension, without replacing any subscheme by its reduction.

The morphism $F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply [lem-trf-unramified-field-fibre-decomposition] separately to $F$ and $Z$: each is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of $k$. Every such extension is $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-alg-closed-finite-extension-trivial]. The finite-type hypothesis makes $C$ quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Both $F$ and $Z$ are closed subschemes, so their underlying spaces are quasi-compact: add the open complement to any open cover and take a finite subcover of $C$. Their singleton summands form an open cover, hence only finitely many summands occur. This proves the finite disjoint-union assertions, including the empty union. The two images are disjoint because the marking is smooth and step 2 identifies the support of $Z$ with the nonsmooth locus.

source.place: Morphisms Tag 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field)(1); Fields Tag 09GR (lemma-algebraically-closed); elementary finite-subcover argument

proof.text: For either $H=F$ or $H=Z$, write the result of step 3 over $k$ as $H\cong\coprod_{a\in I_H}\operatorname{Spec}k$, with $I_H$ finite. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-constant-base-change] with $U=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}L$ and $E=I_H$. It identifies $H_L$ with $\coprod_{a\in I_H}\operatorname{Spec}L$, compatibly with every summand and the projection to $H$. In particular exactly one point $a_L$ lies over each $a\in H$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $F_L$, $Z_L$ and $R_L$ embed as closed subschemes of $C_L$. Distinct points within either special subscheme stay distinct by these embeddings; points from $F_L$ and $Z_L$ cannot coincide because their projections lie in the disjoint original images. Thus $a\mapsto a_L$ is a bijection from $F\cup|Z|$ to $F_L\cup|Z_L|$, with the projection to $C$ sending $a_L$ to $a$.

Fix $a\in F\cup|Z|$ and let $s_a:\operatorname{Spec}k\to C$ be its summand map from step 3. If $a\in|R|$, [lem-weil-pbc-field-point-factors-through-closed-immersion] applied to $R\hookrightarrow C$ factors $s_a$ through $R$. This factorization is over $k$, since its composite with $R\to C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the original structural map. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] then gives a map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to R_L$ whose composite into $C_L$ is the scalar extension of $s_a$; its point is $a_L$ by step 4. Hence $a_L\in|R_L|$. Conversely, if $a_L$ lies on $R_L$, project its point in $R_L$ to $R$ and then to $C$. The pullback square shows its image is $a$, so $a\in|R|$. The incidence equivalence therefore uses no claim about normalization or branches, and applies in fact to any closed subscheme $R$ with the stated scalar extension.

source.place: Schemes Tag 0356 (lemma-map-into-reduction), specialized to Spec k, and the fibre-product universal property

proof.text: Restrict the finite bijection $a\mapsto a_L$ of step 4 to the points lying on $R$. The forward implication in step 5 places its image on $R_L$; the reverse implication shows that the inverse image of any special point on $R_L$ lies on $R$. This is a bijection $R\cap(F\cup|Z|)\simeq R_L\cap(F_L\cup|Z_L|)$, giving the required equality of cardinalities. It counts underlying points, so a self-node contributes one element even when it has two branches. Empty special sets or empty intersections give the empty bijection. Every construction used closed immersions and scalar extension, with no properness or separatedness assumption.

source.place: Conclusion of the rational-point incidence argument; elementary restriction of a finite bijection

Every hypothesis matches the node and none is stronger: IsPureDimension is vacuous on the empty scheme; nonsmooth is written as Mathlib's smoothLocus condition (equal by definition, smoothLocus needs an lfp instance not available here); the ring-iso completion condition is equivalent to the k-algebra one at closed points; Z is the existing firstFittingIdealSheaf subscheme; F is a closed immersion with Etale (i ≫ f) and smooth image. All conclusion clauses are rendered: finite Spec k coproducts with the same index sets after extension to L and summand-wise projection compatibility, disjointness, support of the actual Z_L equals the nonsmooth locus of C_L, BijOn of the projection on special points, incidence iff and Nat.card equality for reduced components whose extension is a reduced component. Edge cases covered: empty C, empty marking, smooth C, L = k, char 2, non-separated C. Single universe u. Advisory only: the helper repeats pullback.map, which also exists as flatClosedFamilyBaseChangeImmersion and closedIdealBaseChangeMap in theorem-node modules (citing those would add a theorem stmt_dep, H2), so the local helper is acceptable. No compile run and no files changed.
